You are an expert at solving ARC-AGI (Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus) puzzles using Answer Set Programming (ASP).

ARC-AGI puzzles show input-output grid transformations. Each cell contains a color value (integer 0–9). The goal is to discover the hidden transformation rule from training examples and encode it as an ASP program.
</context>

<rules>
- `input(row, col, color)` facts are injected automatically — do not define them.
- `color(0..9)` facts are injected automatically — do not define them.
- the output predicate is always `output(row, col, color)` — do not redefine it.
- the final program must produce exactly one answer set, in which `output(row, col, color)` match the expected output exactly.
- end your program with `#show output/3.`
</rules>

<example_1>
This puzzle copies the input to the output unchanged.

<grid_1>
Input:
<diagram>
0 1 0
2 0 3
0 4 0
</diagram>

Output:
<diagram>
0 1 0
2 0 3
0 4 0
</diagram>
</grid_1>

<asp>
% Grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.
row(0..N-1) :- n_rows(N).
col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

% Output has the same dimensions as the input
output_cell(R, C) :- row(R), col(C).

% Each output cell gets exactly one color
1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Copy each input cell to the output unchanged
output(R, C, Color) :- input(R, C, Color).

#show output/3.
</asp>
</example_1>

<asp>
% Grid dimensions

n_cols(N) :- N = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.

col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

% Each output cell gets exactly one color

% Mirror: column C of the output is column (M-1-C) of the input.

#show output/3.
</asp>

% Determine grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(M) :- M = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.
row(0..N-1) :- n_rows(N).
col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

output_cell(R,C) :- row(R), col(C).

1 { output(R,C,Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R,C).

% Detect a non‑zero to the left of a candidate column L
left_of(R,L) :- input(R,C,V2), V2 != 0, C < L.

% Ensure the leftmost pivot has no non‑zero to its left
:- left_of(R,L), leftmost(R,L,V).

% The pivot (leftmost non‑zero) of a row
leftmost(R,L,V) :- input(R,L,V), V != 0, not left_of(R,L).

% Output at the pivot cell

% Zeros left of the pivot (these columns stay zero)

% Distance (number of columns strictly after the pivot up to C)
dist(R,C,L,Dist) :- col(C), col(L), Dist = #count{ X : col(X), X > L, X <= C }.

% After the pivot: odd distance → 5, even distance (>0) → original value V

output(R,C,V)  :- leftmost(R,L,V), dist(R,C,L,Dist), Dist = 2*X, Dist != 0.

output_exists(R) :- leftmost(R,_,_).   % true exactly when a pivot exists

output(R,C,0) :- row(R), col(C), input(R,C,0), not output_exists(R).

%  Grid dimensions
% ------------------------------------------------------------------
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.

% ------------------------------------------------------------------
%  Determine the leftmost non‑zero cell of each row (the “pivot”)
% ------------------------------------------------------------------
left_of(R,L) :- input(R,C,V2), V2 != 0, C < L.

%  The pivot must be the smallest column that contains a non‑zero
%  (i.e. no non‑zero to its left)
:- left_of(R,L), leftmost(R,L,V).

leftmost(R,L,V) :- input(R,L,V), V != 0, \+ left_of(R,L).   % L is the leftmost column

% ------------------------------------------------------------------

n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(M) :- M = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.

output_cell(R, C) :- row(R), col(C).

% ------------ Determine pivot (leftmost non-zero) ----------
pivot(R, P, V) :-
    input(R, P, V), V != 0,
    #count{ Q : col(Q), Q < P, row(R), input(R, Q, X), X != 0 } = 0.

% ------------ Row has no non-zero ----------
no_nonzero_row(R) :-
    row(R),
    #count{ C, X : col(C), row(R), input(R, C, X), X != 0 } = 0.

% ------------ Output the pivot unchanged ----------
output(R, P, V) :- pivot(R, P, V).

% ------------ Cells left of pivot stay zero ----------
output(R, C, 0) :-
    pivot(R, P, V),
    col(C),
    C < P,
    input(R, C, 0).

% ------------ Cells right of pivot: compute distance ----------
dist(P, C, D) :-
    col(P), col(C),
    D = #count{ X : col(X), X > P, X <= C }.

    dist(P, C, D),

    D = 2 * Y,
    D != 0.

% ------------ Rows without any non‑zero: all zero ----------

n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(M) :- M = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.
row(0..N-1) :- n_rows(N).
col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

output_cell(R,C) :- row(R), col(C).

1 { output(R,C,Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R,C).

% ---------- Determine leftmost non‑zero (pivot) ----------
pivot(R,P,V) :-
    input(R,P,V), V != 0,
    #count{ Q : col(Q), Q < P, row(R), input(R,Q,X), X != 0 } = 0.

% ---------- Row with no non‑zero cells ----------
no_nonzero_row(R) :-
    row(R),
    #count{ C,X : col(C), row(R), input(R,C,X), X != 0 } = 0.

% ---------- Output the pivot unchanged ----------

% ---------- Cells left of the pivot ----------
output(R,C,0) :-
    pivot(R,P,V),
    col(C),
    C < P,
    input(R,C,0).

% ---------- Distance from pivot ----------
dist(P,C,D) :-
    col(P), col(C),

% ---------- Cells right of the pivot (odd distance) ----------

    dist(P,C,D),
    D = 2*Y,
    D != 0.

% ---------- Rows without any non‑zero: output all zeros ----------

    no_nonzero_row(R),
    col(C).

% Grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(M) :- M = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.
row(0..N-1) :- n_rows(N).
col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

output_cell(R,C) :- row(R), col(C).

1 { output(R,C,Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R,C).

% Determine leftmost non‑zero (pivot)
pivot(R,P,V) :-
    input(R,P,V), V != 0,
    #count{ Q : col(Q), Q < P, row(R), input(R,Q,X), X != 0 } = 0.

% Row without any non‑zero cell
no_nonzero_row(R) :-
    row(R),
    #count{ C,X : col(C), row(R), input(R,C,X), X != 0 } = 0.

% Output pivot unchanged
output(R,P,V) :- pivot(R,P,V).

% Cells left of the pivot
output(R,C,0) :-
    pivot(R,P,V),
    col(C),
    C < P,
    input(R,C,0).

% Distance from pivot
dist(P,C,D) :-
    col(P), col(C),
    D = C - P.

% Right of pivot, odd distance → colour 5
output(R,C,5) :-
    pivot(R,P,V),
    col(C),
    C > P,
    dist(P,C,D),
    D = 2*Y + 1.

% Right of pivot, even distance (>0) → colour = pivot value
output(R,C,V) :-
    pivot(R,P,V),
    col(C),
    C > P,
    dist(P,C,D),
    D = 2*Y,
    D != 0.

% Rows with no non‑zero cells: output all zeros
output(R,C,0) :-
    no_nonzero_row(R),
    col(C).
